title: Stephen of Hungary (16 August)
hook: the king Hungarians remember as their first Christian king

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pontian and Hippolytus, a pope and his rival at peace in the mines. Your line was reconciled in the mines.

In a parliament building in Budapest, under guard, sits a golden crown. Enamel pictures of saints. Pearls hanging on little chains. And on top, a small cross that sits crooked, bent at an angle, and nobody has straightened it. Hungarians call it the Holy Crown, and they link it to the name of one king. For a long time, tradition says, no one counted as king of Hungary unless crowned with it. Today, the man whose name the crown carries.
screen: `A GOLDEN CROWN UNDER GUARD.` → `A CROOKED CROSS.` → `ONE KING'S NAME.`

segments.voice: Stephen was born the son of a Magyar ruler, at a time when his people were turning from their old gods. Tradition says he was baptized young and took the name Stephen. When he came to power, he wanted to be a Christian king, and tradition says he asked the pope for his blessing and received a crown. Hungarians remember him as their first Christian king. He built churches and organized the Church across his land. He also had to fight to hold it together, and the stories don't pretend he was gentle with every rival. One personal thing he left is a letter of advice to his son, Emeric, which tradition keeps as Stephen's admonitions. As it's usually summarized, he tells his son to keep the faith, to pray, to be patient and merciful, to listen to good counsel, and to welcome strangers, because they bring new gifts to a land. A king writing to the boy who would be king after him. Then grief. Emeric died young, before his father. Stephen, with no heir, is said to have offered his crown and his people to Mary. So the crown is the thread. A crown is power. It can also be a promise, given in trust and handed on. The scriptures speak of another kind of crown, the one at the end of a faithful life. In the Douay-Rheims, Paul writes: "there is laid up for me a crown of justice." Stephen wore one crown, and tradition says he hoped for the other.
screen: `A RULER'S SON, BAPTIZED.` · `A CROWN AND A KINGDOM.` · `ADVICE TO HIS SON.` · `A CROWN HANDED TO MARY.` · then, large: `A CROWN OF JUSTICE.`

segments.voice: Bring Hungary to mind, its towns and rivers, its people getting up this morning for work and school; you don't have to know much, just keep them company. If you pray, pray for its people, its leaders and its families; if you don't, wish them well, breath by breath. If Hungary feels far away, add the place you live, and hold both.
Admonitions. The letter of advice Stephen, Hungary's first Christian king, wrote to his son Emeric, telling him to keep the faith, be patient and merciful, and welcome strangers.
Your line: the holy crown. Some of what we hold is only ours to keep for someone else. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics may keep the optional memorial of Saint Stephen of Hungary on 16 August; in Hungary his feast is kept on 20 August as a national holiday.

A code of laws ordering every stranger to be sent out of Hungary.
